nodes.title: Adversarial review of the reply door, caller signals, voice runtime, compile, calls hook/analysis and Operator: 13 findings (6 blocker, 6 major, 1 minor), each with a failing test. Blockers: plain AI denials pass both doors (B1); any 'AI/bot' token counts as disclosure (B2); a rule split over two sentences passes (B3); 'Hello? Kaun?' confirms identity (B4); a per-contact amount leaks before identity when spelled without the rupee mark (B5); common Hinglish and all Tamil-English crisis lines missed (B6). Majors: amounts in words (M1), Python door ASCII-only \s and case folding vs TS (M2), S2S audio played before its transcript is doored and beta stack not gated (M3), brain cost metered 0 on blocked/withdrawn OpenAI-compatible streams (M4), draft continues after an RD2/RD3 replacement (M5), outcome evidenced by the agent's own line (M6). Verified: ~130 fuzz lines through both doors, sim calls, a LiveSession replay, an HttpBrain stream with fake HTTP, analysis on Postgres with a fake model; all 34 tests fail on their assertion. Not verified: live providers, audio, real Live message order.
Fix the 6 blockers of the what-she-says review before any live call (B1-B6), then M1-M6; promote candidate vectors into cases.json (safety builder decides).
nodes.closes_when: product/voice/tests/test_review.py and product/tests/review/what-she-says.test.ts report unexpected successes for every B and M finding and their markers are dropped
